result.title: Inference-Time Steering Across Scaffolds and Epitopes for Sample-Efficient De Novo Nanobody Design
result.summary: Generative molecular design typically relies on over-generation and post-hoc filtering. Inference-time steering methods like Feynman-Kac (FK) steering improve efficiency by biasing trajectories toward high-reward candidates, yet they optimize within a single fixed configuration. In de novo nanobody design, upfront commitment to conditioning choices like scaffold identity or target epitope creates a bottleneck. Since yield varies across these conditions, steering unpromising setups wastes compute. We recast generative condition selection as an inference-time resource-allocation problem. We propose two dynamic budget allocators: a joint Global Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) formulation that steers and allocates compute across configurations concurrently, and a decoupled approach adapting Batched Successive Elimination (BaSE). Empirically, these dynamic allocators increase the yield of designable candidates per GPU-hour nearly 5$\times$ without sacrificing diversity across distinct therapeutic targets and generative configurations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 de novo 纳米抗体设计中对 scaffold、epitope 等条件的前置选择重述为推理期资源分配问题，提出联合式 Global SMC 与解耦式 BaSE 两种动态预算分配器，在多个治疗靶点上将每 GPU 小时的可设计候选产出提高近 5 倍且不牺牲多样性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其序贯蒙特卡洛轨迹偏置与逐步淘汰式预算分配，可能为 LVR 中多假设 latent 轨迹的计算分配、视觉证据筛选与停止决策提供远领域类比，具体对应关系需核查。
